description: ZALF documented soil variability at 80 grid points across a 20-hectare agricultural field in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. Each point was sampled to 90 centimetres. Across 1999–2002, the dataset records soil moisture and mineral nitrogen before sowing and after harvest, along with texture, organic carbon, field management and annual yield. The named public ZALF GeoNode resource opened; DataCite lists CSV and CC BY-NC 4.0, with no fee indicated. Water and crop modellers can use the grid to test spatially variable soil and irrigation inputs or calibrate soil-water and nutrient simulations. This one field does not show how the same relationships vary across farms or climates. Sampling is seasonal for some measures, not a continuous sensor stream. No CSV was downloaded, and a direct file link was not confirmed from the map-style landing page. This resource is related to the broader international soil-hydraulic collection G4-0577 but measures spatial variation within one field. The full local duplicate scan found no catalogue identity match.
